summary: A detailed critique of Citadel Securities documenting 58 FINRA regulatory violations, tracking the firm's short position growth to $57.5 billion in 2020 (a 127.57% year-over-year increase), and arguing that Fair Value accounting will force Citadel to mark losses as GME prices rise. The author cites the March 10, 2021 flash crash as evidence of market manipulation and predicts an imminent financial crisis for the firm. While the factual data (regulatory fines, balance sheet figures, payment-for-order-flow practices) comes from primary sources, the core thesis that Citadel faces collapse and that a short squeeze is imminent remains speculative.

key_claims.claim: Claims that Citadel Securities has been fined 58 times by FINRA for regulatory violations including naked shorting and trading ahead of customer orders
key_claims.note: FINRA records cited with specific violation dates and fine amounts; naked shorting violations (pages 5, 11) and trading-ahead violations (page 10) documented.

key_claims.claim: Claims that Citadel Securities' short position increased 127.57% year-over-year in 2020 to $57.5 billion
key_claims.note: Based on Citadel Securities' published financial statements for 2018-2020 (pages 5-8); documented liability balances.

key_claims.claim: Claims that Fair Value accounting will force Citadel to mark short positions to current market price, creating unsustainable losses as GME rises
key_claims.note: Fair Value accounting principle correctly described (pages 8-9); however, this did not result in Citadel collapse (hindsight).

key_claims.claim: Claims that the March 10, 2021 flash crash (40% drop in 25 minutes) was orchestrated market manipulation by Citadel and coordinated with media
key_claims.note: Flash crash occurred (verified); attribution to Citadel and proof of deliberate coordination not substantiated by any regulator through 2026. Author acknowledges uncertainty (page 15).

key_claims.claim: Claims that Citadel will face margin call pressure and collapse as short losses mount due to rising GME price
key_claims.note: Citadel was never margin-called and remains a major market maker through 2026 (hindsight fact); this prediction failed.

key_claims.claim: Claims that SRCC 801 rule means DTCC does not hold retail investors' physical shares
key_claims.note: SRCC 801 concerns central counterparty clearing mechanics, not retail share custody model. Rule is mischaracterized (page 17).

key_claims.claim: Claims that payment for order flow from Robinhood to Citadel is undisclosed and gives Citadel unfair advantage in trading
key_claims.note: PFOF practices documented; EU later banned PFOF by 2026. Conflict of interest is real (page 4).

key_claims.claim: Claims that an imminent financial crisis (the 'sh*tsunami') will force shorts to cover and trigger a massive squeeze
key_claims.note: No MOASS occurred; GME peaked ~$65 May 2024 (vs. $483 intraday Jan 2021); short interest normalized to ~20% by Feb 2021.

validity_rationale: The book's factual claims about regulatory violations, financial statement figures, and payment-for-order-flow practices are grounded in primary sources (FINRA records, Citadel Securities filings) and check out against the documented record. Market mechanics (Fair Value accounting, high-frequency trading practices) are described accurately. However, the core thesis—that Citadel faces margin call and collapse, and that an imminent squeeze will ensue—is falsified by hindsight: Citadel was never margin-called, remained solvent, and continued as a major market maker. The book makes significant unproven inferential leaps from accurate data (short position amounts, regulatory history) to speculative conclusions about conspiracy and imminent financial crisis. Some claims are mischaracterized (SRCC 801). The predicted timeline for a squeeze never materialized.
